[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: 'print a' should show what is in a, as when you print a list on paper. Java rule: System.out.println(a) converts the reference to text such as [I@bf3f7e0 (type code plus hexadecimal hash/address) and never reads the elements.
[1] misconception (M) -> ArrayPrintsContents: wrong rule: System.out.println(a) prints the elements of the array a. Right rule: Printing an array variable prints its memory address (a hexadecimal integer like @f62373), not its elements.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> ArrayPrintsContents: Points to LT: println(a) converts the one reference value to a String; no traversal happens. Inconsistent application: the trace prints the elements for one println(a) but an address for another. (here mixing in: "System.out.println(a) prints the elements of the array a")

[0] names_the_element (N): Identity: printing an array variable outputs the text form of its reference ([I@..., [D@...), not a listing of the elements.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Declarative: any value, including an array reference, is converted to a String when printed or concatenated; for an array this string is its type code and address.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Sequencing: the argument a is evaluated to a reference, string conversion turns it into text, and println writes that text and a newline. The elements are never read.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Result: one line such as [I@bf3f7e0 for an int[] ([D@... for double[]); the hex part changes from run to run. Exception: println(char[]) has its own overload and prints the characters.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): State transition: no variable or element changes; only one line of output is produced.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Two aliases print the same text, and two separately created arrays with equal contents print different text, because println shows the reference that assignment and == also act on.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan/role: useful only as a diagnostic of identity (do two names hold the same reference?). To show the contents, traverse and print each a[i], or print Arrays.toString(a).

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> ArrayPrintsContents: Conservation: changing the elements does not change what println(a) prints (the same array keeps its reference). Replacing println(a) by a loop or Arrays.toString(a) changes the output to the elements.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Applicability: print a reference only when debugging whether two names share an array. For output of values use an element loop (one per line or formatted) or Arrays.toString.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: println of an array reference prints the reference, not the elements. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: an array variable (not an element) is passed to print/println or concatenated, as in "a = " + a, expecting the values
wrong: System.out.println(a) prints the elements of the array a. | right: Printing an array variable prints its memory address (a hexadecimal integer like @f62373), not its elements.
Both follow from the array variable holding a reference (memory address): assignment and == act on that reference, and println(a) prints it.
Printing an array variable prints the reference it holds, not the elements.
println of an array variable prints the array's reference, not its elements.
